hypothesis: The skeleton of a dolphin, read as a cetacean, is bone rather than the spine of a fish.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered, before the spreadsheet was downloaded. Supports if at least one row names a cetacean and at least one numeric column whose header refers to bone, cortical bone, an osteon or bone volume has a value greater than zero on that row. Cetacean genera accepted, and no others: Delphinus, Tursiops, Stenella, Phocoena, Orcinus, Globicephala, Grampus, Lagenorhynchus, Sousa, Steno, Cephalorhynchus, Phocoenoides, Neophocaena, Balaenoptera, Megaptera, Balaena, Eubalaena, Physeter, Kogia, Ziphius, Mesoplodon, Hyperoodon, Monodon, Delphinapterus, Inia, Lipotes, Platanista, Pontoporia. A common name of dolphin, porpoise or whale in the species cell also counts. A zero or a blank is not a positive bone measurement.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refutes if every cetacean row is labeled cartilage or fish-spine, or if the only tissue values on cetacean rows are explicit zeros in the bone columns. Inconclusive, reason underpowered, if the file loads and contains no cetacean row. Inconclusive, reason not-operationalizable, if the file loads and has no numeric bone, cortical, osteon or bone-volume column. Inconclusive, reason data-unavailable, if the file cannot be retrieved.

test_contract.expected_observation: Cetacean ribs, humeri or vertebrae in the histology table carry a positive measurement of bone.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The cetacean skeletal elements in the table are labeled cartilage or fish-spine, or their bone measurements are explicit zeros.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: The supplementary workbook named by figshare as the bone-histology tables for cetacean rib, humerus and vertebrae: article 10049012, DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.10049012.v1, file 12862_2019_1509_MOESM1_ESM.xlsx (106953 bytes in the article metadata), download https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/18111446. The metadata was read on 2026-11-02 UTC. The workbook was not downloaded before this registration. No second file may be added after the sheet is read.
test_contract.inference_method: Read every sheet. A cetacean row is one whose species cell starts with an accepted genus or contains dolphin, porpoise or whale. A bone column is a numeric column whose header matches bone, cortical, osteon or bone volume, and not a gene-name column of dN/dS values. Supports if any cetacean row has a value greater than zero in any bone column. Refutes only on an explicit cartilage or fish-spine label, or on explicit zeros. Otherwise inconclusive, with the reason in fail_criterion.

interpretation: Aristotle's 'fish-spine' is the skeletal material he contrasts with bone. The scope line reads the dolphin as a cetacean, so a bone measurement on a cetacean skeleton is in scope, not only the genus Delphinus. A positive histological measurement of bone is the observation that the element is bone. The test does not compare a dolphin with a particular fish species, and it does not claim that every cetacean bone is solid rather than spongy.
caveats: The workbook was not opened before this file was committed. The byte size is the size reported by the figshare API, not a hash of the body.
The genus list is a taxonomic gate so that an outgroup in the same workbook is not counted. It is not a result.
Gene dN/dS columns, if present, are not bone measurements and are excluded by the header rule.
